drawings.notes: Three figures in the right column. (1) A pencil of about ten pencil lines through s, one in red from F to F'; legends X_0 and (n=5). (2) Two disks ringed in yellow, each carrying a red pseudoline arrangement, now redrawn strand by strand from the 400 dpi facsimile: in each disk two strands join the two black points at the ends of the horizontal diameter (a lens), and further strands (five in the upper disk, four in the lower) cross the disk; every pair crosses exactly once inside its disk (the two lens strands meet only at the two points); a thick black bar at the bottom of each disk, just inside the rim. The strands are drawn to the rim, where several of them stop a little short on the page; the thin pencil line along the inside of the yellow rims, the short blue pencil stroke by the right point of the upper disk are left out; the pencil arc outside the lower disk on the left is drawn. The word « ou » between the two disks is not visible on the facsimile at this place. (3) A yellow arc (the face F_i, « face supercritique ») carrying three fans of strokes, with arrows from « faces sous-stables » and « faces stables »; legend X_1. Still differs from the facsimile: in (3) the pencil strokes below the arc are left out. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): « In the lower disk, do the two strands meeting near the bottom cross or only touch? » Two pseudo-lines of an arrangement cross exactly once, so the two strands that meet near the bottom cross: as drawn. drawings.notes: A small disk with a yellow-green rim, red dots just inside it (the « bord pointillé de rouge »), crossed by an arrangement of five red pseudolines, redrawn strand by strand from the 400 dpi facsimile (ray positions read off the colour mask): each pseudoline continues outside the rim as two straight red rays, so ten red rays, and between two consecutive red rays there are exactly two yellow rays (twenty yellow rays, thirty rays in all; the earlier count « about 28 » and « alternately » corrected). Each pseudoline joins two opposite red rays (fifth to fifth in the cyclic order), and every pair of the five crosses exactly once inside the disk (10 crossings, computed on the drawn curves); the ray ends on the rim are the intersections of the fitted ray lines with the rim. Near the centre two strands from the top touch before crossing (a tight knot on the page); they are drawn close and crossing once. Legend X'_1 pour n = 5. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): « Near the centre, two strands from the top make a tight knot: one crossing, or a touch and then a crossing? » Two pseudo-lines cross exactly once, so the knot is one crossing: as drawn. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): « How many rays are there, and how do red and yellow alternate? » Counted again round the disk: 10 red rays, which is what n = 5 pseudolines give (two ends each), and 20 yellow-green rays, two between neighbouring red rays everywhere. As drawn. Not checked by a reader.

Top: the yellow line D; a pencil of three orange lines through one vertex (the intersection of the two outer lines, the third drawn through it); the specialisation D' dotted in yellow-green, starting on D and rising through the vertex, down again on the right; the two dark bars across the pencil (dashed blue-green above the vertex, black below it) and the thick blue-green segment just above D, each ending on the two outer lines of the pencil; the two small vertical arrows; further right an orange cross whose two lines meet on D. Foot of the page: D in yellow, two solid brown lines along it (above and below), two dashed brown arcs over the vertex (the outer one from the upper brown line to the upper brown line, the inner one from the lower brown line to the lower brown line, ends computed on those lines); the pencil of three orange lines through one computed vertex, D' dotted in yellow-green from D through the vertex back to D; the three thick black bars are the pieces of the outer arc, of the inner arc and of the upper brown line between the two outer lines of the pencil; arrows to sigma (the bar on the upper brown line) and sigma' (the inner arc); the short blue dotted stroke under the vertex, below the lower brown line, now drawn; an orange cross on the left, a single stroke and a cross on the right, whose lines meet on D. Margin: two small stars of yellow-green pseudolines (each two strands through one vertex, plus a third short stroke at D' under the black arrow a'), joined by the orange arrow from the vertex at D to the vertex at D'; the blue dotted arcs (alpha', beta' at D', alpha, beta at D) drawn as arcs centred on the vertices, from one strand to the other; the yellow dotted ray a' below D on the line from the vertex. The lower marginal point is labelled a' on the facsimile. Questions settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): (1) in the star at D the black point is the vertex: the four strand ends converge within half a millimetre of it and the arrow to the vertex at D′ starts there; (2) the lower marginal label is a′ (clear prime stroke; the plain a is the letter beside the arrow between the stars), against « a » in the transcription; (3) at the foot the outer dashed arc leaves and rejoins the upper brown line, the inner one goes down through the upper line and D to the lower brown line on both sides. drawings.kind: line with two crossings and a numbered contour; curve passing through a crossing; crossing straddled by curves; crossing with two green curves
drawings.notes: Left, colour and pencil drawings, every line read on the 400 dpi crop. Top: a light green line through the crossing points of two crossings of red lines (the crossings computed and the line drawn through them), running on in pencil to an arrow; two black bars along the line on either side, from the right leg of the first crossing to the left leg of the second (ends computed on the legs); an arrowed dark green contour leaving the line at a node on the left and coming back to it on the right (both nodes on the line), with a dark green arc across the bars; arcs and regions numbered 3, 1 (top, bottom), 3, 1 (left), 4, 2 (right), 4. Middle: a red horizontal line, two red verticals, a red arch from the bottom of a third vertical over to the right vertical (ending on it), a red diagonal from the top down to the lower pencil curve (ending on it); two pencil curves, arrowed at both ends, the upper one rising before the arch and the lower one after it and merging into the upper one, the region between them hatched (bounded by the two curves and closed on the left where the hatching starts). Bottom: a red horizontal line, a red vertical meeting it at a black dot (computed), two red lines crossing at a black dot (computed); a pencil bell curve over the crossing, reinforced in black at the top and on the right; an inner pencil curve partly dashed in black, a black arc, an arrowed pencil curve across the crossing and a pencil curve below; regions numbered 1 to 7. Bottom right: a red horizontal and vertical, two red lines crossing, a dark green bell curve, a light green curve and a dashed dark green curve. Right: two pencil disks (an asterisk in the upper one) and the two edges of the pencil ribbon running up to the right. The large ink blots in the middle of the sheet are stains, not drawings. Redrawn further pass (issue 128). Still differs from the facsimile: the pencil ribbon is drawn only by two edges placed by eye, without its twist into the disk and its inner strokes; the pencil sketch at the top right, the faint pencil lens curves inside the top contour, the faint pencil lines round the middle and bottom figures, the small pencil arrows and the doubtful marks (« 7 », « 4 » with arrows in the top contour, a second « 4 » under the 2 at the bottom) are left out; the hatching is drawn as a pattern, not stroke by stroke. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): « Are the arrowed marks inside the top contour « 7 » and « 4 », and is there a second « 4 » under the 2 in the bottom figure? » They are on the page and are now drawn: a crossed 7 with small arrows above the bars inside the top contour (the 4 below the bars was already drawn), and a second 4 under the 2 of the bottom figure. Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): « Do the two crossings lie on the light green line? » On it: both red crossings fall within one stroke width of the light green line, between the two black bars. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.notes: On a printed listing (CRAY2 job banner, 16 Aug 82; not reproduced). Top, in colour: a dark green line blackened between two crossings of red lines, the crossings computed and placed on the line (every red line drawn through its crossing), and a dark green ribbon closed round it, its two branches leaving the line at a node on the left and coming back at a node on the right (nodes on the line). In pencil, every line read on the 400 dpi crop: a long line arrowed to the left with two dots on it; on it a sketch of lines crossing two by two, two of them meeting at a large dot, with lines through a second dot; a crossing at a dot on the right; a parallelepiped in perspective with its inner diagonals, the inner points computed as meetings of the edges drawn through them; a quadrilateral whose two marked vertices are computed as the crossings of its sides, a diagonal with a marked point and a small arrow; at the bottom, lines crossing two by two, the crossings and the two marked points below computed as meetings of the lines drawn through them, with a long line across; lines through a marked point in the middle; two long lines crossing at a dot on the right; a pencil oval at the top with two strokes inside and a short black arc on it; a pencil sketch at the top right (a long line, a shaded band and V-shaped strokes). Redrawn further pass (issue 128). Still differs from the facsimile: the pencil sketches are many faint strokes, only the legible ones are drawn and some of their ends are placed as read; the dashed arcs and small pencil loops inside the coloured ribbon, the faint lens round the top right sketch, the handwriting on the long arrowed line and several faint long lines across the sheet are left out; the two red crossings of the colour figure lie slightly above the line on the page (here on it). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): « Do the red crossings of the colour figure lie on the blackened line? » On it: each crossing falls inside the thickness of the blackened bar, at its end (0.2 to 0.3 mm above its axis). Not checked by a reader. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): « Is the edge set of the pencil parallelepiped right? » No erased lines are seen: all strokes are firm pencil. Two edges are corrected on the 400 dpi crop: the stroke from the left vertex goes to the marked point of the left face and on to the inner bottom vertex (not to the centre point), and the stroke from the inner bottom vertex to the bottom right vertex is added (26 edges). Not checked by a reader.

Below: an inked circle with ticks, lettered u, v, x* along the top, a dot x and a circled -1 inside the lower left, and under it an arc tangent to the circle at its lowest point, with a dot and x + 1, and u' at the right. Middle, colour: four light green arcs (an arch, a U, an arch, a U) with light green blobs at their ends and at the joins; on each side a red cross with a short blue stroke beside it, lettered epsilon', epsilon''; a third red cross with a dark dot at the top of the first and third arcs and at the lower left of the fourth; red ticks along the first two arcs (eight and ten); the ends u, v and u', v'; braces alpha', alpha'' on the shoulders of the first arc, a letter read gamma above its top cross, and a brace alpha' + alpha'' + gamma under the second; signs + under the top crosses of the first and third arcs, - by the third cross of the fourth; a double arrow between the first and second arcs and between the third and fourth. Not certain: beside the first arc, a bold sign read as a multiplication cross at (67.5,-11.8) and a pencil letter read gamma at (77,-12.3); the tick lettered at (52,-137.5) on the right of the circle carries a mark like C or 0, not drawn; a struck scribble under the circle at (36.5,-162) and a struck label at its left (22,-150) are left out, as are the smudges and the large faint erased circle around the inked one. The inequalities written at the right belong to the text. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 128, Claude claude-opus-5-5): redraw compiled with tectonic and laid over the 402 ppi colour scan; the whole figure sat about 0.5 mm left of and above the ink, and was moved by (+0.55, -0.5). Added: in the U (second coloured arc) the thin blue-grey line that carries the red ticks, from the cross epsilon' down to the bottom blob and up to the cross epsilon'', just outside the light green U (the ticks and crosses sit on it, not on the green). Checked and unchanged: both pencil eights (circles, spindles, dots, crossing strokes, dashed arcs), the inked circle with u, v, x*, x, circled -1, x + 1, u', the four coloured arcs, crosses, ticks, blue strokes, braces and double arrows. Still differs: the large faint erased circle around the inked one and the erased marks on it are not drawn (erased, not struck); the mark like C or 0 at the tick right of x*, a small « s » beside the top cross of the first arch, the struck scribble under the circle and the smudges are left out.

drawings.kind: circle with a crown of dashed petals
drawings.notes: Redrawn from a 400 dpi colour crop, coordinates read on gridded crops and the redraw checked on an overlay. The circle is not a plain circle: it is a ring of sixteen vertices, its sides alternately a straight bar (dark green outside, blue inside; eight) and a lens of two light green arcs (eight). A radial bar, dark green and blue, stands outward at each vertex (sixteen), and a dashed light green petal joins the outer ends of consecutive radial bars (sixteen petals, not thirteen). The petals are traced from a page view at a coarser grid than the rest and their outlines are approximate; on the page neighbouring petals overlap near the bar ends, which the redraw simplifies. Upper four sections, in red: over the upper left bar two arcs and a row of short strokes standing on the bar; three arcs numbered 5, 6, 7 that leave that bar inside the ring, cross the next lens and end above it; over the first lens an arc to a many-rayed knot and two yellow wedges against the radial bars; over the top bar four nested arches numbered 3, 2, 1, 0 at both feet, strokes standing on the bar numbered 7, 6, 5, 4 below it, and three dashed arcs and one solid arc sweeping under the bar to the right-hand lens; over the second lens two knots joined by an arc, strokes down to the vertices, two yellow wedges, the numbers 0, 1, 2, 3 in the wedge and 4, 5, 6 on the lens. Inside the ring, at the other bars: short red strokes with their numbers (6, 5; 4; 1, 2, 3; 7; 6, 5; 4), pencil lines to the pencil numbers 7', 5', 6', 4, 3', 2', 1', 7, 5, 6, 4, 3, 2, 1, and the rotation arrow at the centre; three pencil rotation arrows over the upper sections. Right, in pencil: a disk with a spindle of three arcs from top to bottom and five chords; below it an oval with a knot at the top (0, 1, 2, 3 above, 3, 2, 1 below) and one at the bottom (3', 2', 1'), a curl under it. Left: a small pencil star. Still approximate: the short red strokes over the upper left bar and their crossings, which the page overwrites with black scribble (the scribble is not drawn); the rays of the three knots; the numbers written inside the two dark wedges, which are not legible and are left out; a heavy black scribble at the right end of the second lens, which looks like a deletion, is not drawn; the second row of faint pencil numbers above the bottom bar is left out. The row of digits in pencil under the figure is in the transcription and is not drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again. Overlay check 2026-11-13 (issue 128, Claude Opus 5.5): compiled with tectonic, rasterised and laid over the 300 dpi crop of the facsimile.
